To Menoeceus. It reads, word for word and point for point: So death, the most terrifying of ills, is nothing to us, since so long as we exist, death is not with us; but when death comes, then we do not exist. The next sentence (It does not then concern either the living or the dead) starts after the full stop, so the cut is clean. The English page falls between Greek pages 84 and 86, so p. 85 is right. The OCR misreads the running head as 88. Attribution: Epicurus's own letter, preserved in Diogenes Laertius X; not on the misattribution list. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Epicurus 1 of 3 (month 1, a different sentence from 122 in Hicks), not banned.
